tasks.title: red-first reads a house case by its full label and the unittest reader only on unittest output
tasks.description: stamp-verification.failing_cases takes label.split()[0] as a house case's id, so a label that is a sentence starting with an ordinary word ('the', 'a') gets an id that also exists in HEAD's test file and the task's own case is never recognised; and _UNITTEST_CASE (^(FAIL|ERROR): ) is applied to every output, so a house suite whose PASSING case prints 'ERROR: <path> is not a directory' as expected stdout gets a phantom failing case. Reported on P78.9 (a new house case 'the gate-economy row is wired into diagnose() ...' read could-not-prove, exit 3, while the raw run had exactly that one FAIL line). Fix: a house case is identified by its FULL label, with a leading id-shaped token (letters then digits, e.g. me1, ga9b) used as its id only when present; the task's own case is matched by either; the unittest FAIL:/ERROR: reader applies only when the output is unittest-shaped (a 'Ran N tests' line). Cases both ways: a sentence label proves red, an id-led label is still named by its id, a house run with an expected ERROR: line counts no phantom, a real unittest ERROR: is still counted and not credited as an assertion.

outcome.descriptive: Red-first proof now recognises a task's own test whose name is a sentence, and no longer mistakes a passing test's printed error message for a failure.

tasks.title: Review findings: red-first reads only the runner that ran, and a label is judged by the most specific literal that renders it
tasks.description:
Phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (R1) failing_cases reads only the runner read_tally selected, never another runner whose tally line merely appears in the output; a case with a house run that prints a captured unittest transcript. (R2) a label is the task's own when the MOST SPECIFIC literal in the working tree that renders it (the one with the most fixed characters) is absent from HEAD's literals; a loose template such as '%dx%d' can no longer make a new case unprovable or an edited one proved; cases for both probes. (R3) a FAIL line's detail is set aside at every ' (' whether or not the line ends in ')', so a multi-line detail still matches. (R4) the label matcher is linear: the fixed parts are found in order with str.find, anchored at both ends, no regex backtracking; a case with many placeholders against a long label finishes. (R5) the Usage line, the --case help and audit-executor.md say an id or a full label. (R6) the already-carried refusal uses the same match as the proof, so a pytest nodeid is not called carried when it is not. (R7) the cases above each proven red.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:331-352 (failing_cases): Each runner is gated on its tally appearing ANYWHERE in the output. That is not the runner read_tally() chose. A house run whose passing case prints a captured unittest transcript (a 'Ran N tests' line) still gets unittest FAIL:/ERROR: phantoms, so the phase's own defect survives in that shape. The phantom FAIL: also counts as an assertion. Probe (scratchpad/p82/probe8.py): in the WT test, the existing sentence case was edited to go red, and a new passing case prints 'FAIL: test_new_rule ... Ran 3 tests ...'. `red` exit 0 proved, crediting 'test_new_rule (FAIL)' as the task's own. The only real failing case was the pre-existing one. This is a false proved. -> Read only the runner that read_tally() selects, for example failing_cases(text, runner) called with tally['runner'] from classify_run/red_verdict. Add a case: a house tally plus an echoed unittest transcript names no unittest case and does not prove.
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_pattern: A literal counts as a template when its fixed text holds any single word character. So '%dx%d' becomes .*?x.*?, which renders every label containing an 'x', and '%s is %s' renders every label containing ' is '. probe4 found such a loose literal rendering no-id labels in test__config_rules.py ('%r validates clean') and test_gen_demo_manifest.py ('%dx%d'). End to end (probe5.py): a HEAD test file holding VIEW = '%dx%d' % (1280, 720) makes a genuinely new case 'the fix sets the next value' read could-not-prove (exit 3). The same suite without that literal reads proved (exit 0). This is a false could-not-prove. In the other direction, a loose literal ADDED in WT renders an existing case that HEAD's literals fail to render. Combined with finding 3, probe6.py gives a false proved (exit 0) for an existing case whose condition was edited. The control without the literal gives exit 3. -> Judge by the most specific rendering literal, not by any literal. The case is the task's own when the literal with the most fixed text that renders the label is absent from HEAD's literal set. Alternatively, require the fixed text to anchor the label: no leading placeholder unless the fixed text holds a whole multi-letter word, and never a lone character. Add sr54 rows for '%dx%d' and '%s is %s'.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_forms: The FAIL line's detail is set aside only when the label ends in ')'. A check() detail containing a newline is common: sr48 in this very test file passes text_u[-400:]. Such a detail leaves the FAIL line as 'label (first line of detail', with no closing paren. Then no literal fullmatches, so a genuinely new sentence-labelled case reads could-not-prove. probe5.py: detail 'line one\nline two' gives exit 3 could-not-prove. The single-line control gives exit 0 proved. -> Offer the prefix before each ' (' as a form whether or not the line ends in ')', or at least when it does not. Add a case where a sentence-labelled new case has a multi-line detail.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_pattern / _carries_label: Every placeholder compiles to .*? and is fullmatched against each label form, for every string literal in both copies of the file. A literal that opens with several placeholders separated by short fixed text backtracks combinatorially. probe1.py: '%s '*6+'zq' against a 60-word label took 1.18s, and '%s '*12+'zq' did not finish in 180s. This runs after the red run and is not bounded by --timeout. Over the real tests/ tree it cost about 1.9s total for one long label (probe2.py), so this is latent, not observed. -> Match wildcard templates without a regex engine. Split the literal on placeholders, then check startswith(first piece), endswith(last piece) and find the middle pieces left to right. That is linear and exact for fullmatch. Or cap the placeholder count.

So --case tests/test_x.py::test_a narrows to that failure, and the own check (by id test_a) proves it. The refused check runs on the raw --case string instead. It finds that nodeid in neither file and adds it to refused. The proved basis then says '--case tests/test_x.py::test_a names a case HEAD's test file already carries', which is false. This is found by reading only; there is no pytest probe. -> Resolve each --case name to the failures it names, then run _added_by_task on their id/label rather than on the raw string. tasks.title: Round-2 review findings: an exact literal outranks a template, a run-time label is a template, and two runners tally to could-not-prove
tasks.description:
Round-2 review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (S1) a placeholder-free literal that matches the label exactly outranks any template, the longest such match wins, and templates are consulted only when no exact literal matches; probe9 (a) as a case. (S2) _fold treats a non-literal `+` operand, an f-string field and a .format field as placeholders, so a label built at run time is a template with those parts open; the remaining limit is written into _standing's docstring; probe9 (b) as a case. (S3) when tallies of more than one runner appear, the test command decides when it names the runner (pytest, python -m unittest, a house --selftest); otherwise the verdict is could-not-prove naming both tallies; the read_tally docstring says what it does; probe9 (c) as a case and sr55 follows. (S4) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md describes the runner that ran and the most-specific-literal rule.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:374-423 (_closest_literals, _standing): This is a regression introduced by P82.2, and it gives a false proved. The score for 'most specific' is the total fixed text of any literal that renders ANY form of the label, and that includes the full FAIL line with its detail. Suppose the working tree adds a literal that spells the printed line, such as a test asserting on the harness's output: EXPECT = 'the next value is read (saw %r)'. That literal then outranks HEAD's exact literal 'the next value is read'. The closest literal is not in HEAD, so an EXISTING case whose condition was edited to go red counts as the task's own. Probe scratchpad/p82/probe9.py (a) gives red exit 0 proved. The control with the same edit and no added literal gives exit 3 could-not-prove. P82.1 refused this case, because HEAD's exact literal rendered the label. No sr case covers this shape. -> Rank a placeholder-free literal equal to a form of the label above any template. Among exact renderings, take the longest form. Fall back to the most specific template only when no literal renders the label exactly. That way the detail never outranks the label, and a new parenthetical label ('the value (as read)') still beats an unrelated exact 'the value'. Add probe9 (a) as an sr row and prove it red against the current code.
R2 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:590-602 (_fold), 401-423 (_standing): Limit 1, which the implementer left in place, CAN give a false proved. In the test, an existing case's label is built at run time ('the ' + KIND + ' is read'), so none of HEAD's literals renders it. The working tree edits the case's condition and adds MSG = '%s is %s'. The generic template becomes the closest literal, HEAD does not hold it, and the result is 'added'. probe9 (b) gives exit 0 proved. The control without the template gives exit 3. _standing's docstring does not state this limit. A one-off AST scan found 15 of 9958 check() calls in plugins/audit/tests and tools/ whose label does not fold to a literal, mostly a Name taken from a table, so the exposure in this repo is narrow. I measured that once and it is not a gate. -> Make _fold treat a non-literal operand of '+', an f-string FormattedValue and a '.format' field as a placeholder. HEAD's run-time label then has its own template ('the %s is read'), which outranks a generic one. Write the remaining limit (a label no literal in HEAD spells even partly) into _standing's docstring, and add probe9 (b) as a case.
R3 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:414-420 (read_tally), 528 (red_verdict): Limit 2, which the implementer left in place, CAN give a false proved. It is the mirror image of R1. In a unittest run, the existing test_old was edited to fail, and a new passing test prints 'FAIL zz9 ...' and 'SELFTEST FAILED: 1/2 cases passed'. read_tally takes the house tally first, so the house reader credits zz9, which appears in the working tree's text and not in HEAD's. probe9 (c) gives exit 0 proved on the phantom. Without the echoed tally it gives exit 3, naming test_old. Choosing the runner whose tally prints last does not fix this. Under a merged pipe, the test's buffered stdout lands AFTER unittest's 'Ran 2 tests' and 'FAILED' lines on stderr. I checked this directly: the house lines printed last. The docstring 'The first tally a known runner printed' is also untrue, because the order is a fixed precedence, not print order. P82.2 now leans on it for 'the runner that ran'. -> When the output holds tallies from more than one runner, let the command decide when it names the runner ('-m unittest', 'pytest'). Otherwise fail closed to could-not-prove, with a basis that names both tallies. Correct the read_tally docstring. Add probe9 (c) as a case. sr55 pins house precedence for the reverse shape and would need to follow whichever rule is chosen.
R4 (low) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:3653-3655: P82.1 wrote this and P82.2 left it unchanged. It still says failing_cases reads 'each runner's lines only in output that carries that runner's tally'. That is exactly the behaviour R1 found wrong and P82.2 replaced. The paragraph also says nothing of the most-specific-literal rule that now decides whether a label counts as the task's own. -> Say that failing_cases reads only the lines of the runner whose tally the verdict came from, and that a label counts as the task's own when HEAD does not hold the most specific literal that renders it, matching the CHANGELOG entry.

outcome.technical: Literals ranked by role (case label arguments first), run-time labels folded as templates, mixed tallies are could-not-prove unless the command names the runner.

tasks.title: Round-3 review findings: a disagreement between rankings fails closed, and case-call wrappers are derived exactly
tasks.description:
Round-3 review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (T1) fail closed when the role-first and the role-blind ranking disagree - the case is held by HEAD when HEAD holds the closest literal under EITHER ranking; probe10 (d), (e), (f) as cases, probe9 unchanged, the allow rows still prove; re-check probe11 (k) under the new rule and, if it still proves, close it or name it exactly in _standing's docstring. (T2) _case_callees skips `self`/`cls` for a method wrapper, recognises a keyword label argument and a lambda wrapper, reads a wrapper imported from a sibling test module, and matches a callee by name only for a plain-name call, never an attribute call such as subprocess.run; probe10 (g) as a case. (T3) cases for both surviving mutations: an existing table-fed case edited to fail stays could-not-prove, and a command naming `python -m pytest` picks pytest.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:809-829 (_closest_literals), 841-868 (_standing, incl. the WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE paragraph at 850-855): P82.3 introduced a false proved, and P82.2 did not have it. Ranking by role first means any label-argument TEMPLATE outranks an exact literal from the 'others' role. Take an existing case whose label is not a derived label argument: a table row fed to check by a loop, a method wrapper, or check(label=...). It is edited to go red, and the task adds a PASSING case whose label template renders the existing label, such as check('the next value is %s' % ('x',), True). The new template becomes the closest literal, HEAD does not hold it, and the existing case reads as the task's own. Evidence from scratchpad/p82/probe10.py on HEAD: (d) table label gives exit 0 proved, (e) method wrapper gives exit 0 proved, (f) keyword label gives exit 0 proved. The same edits with no new template are all exit 3: (d0) and (e0), and (e1), the module-level wrapper plus a new template. On an export of P82.2 (f8bbbf6b), (d), (e) and (f) all give exit 3. The docstring's limit says such a label 'is judged among the other literals'. For this shape that is untrue: the label is judged by whichever label-argument template renders it. -> Fail closed when the two rankings disagree. at_head should also be true when HEAD holds the closest literal of the role-blind ranking, _closest_in(wt['labels'] + wt['others'], forms). I tried exactly this on a scratch export. probe10 (d), (e) and (f) gave exit 3. probe9 (a), (b) and (c) were unchanged at exit 3. The allow rows (i) and (g0) still proved, and test_stamp_verification --selftest gave 90/90 with exit 0. Add (d), (d0), (e) and (f) as sr cases and prove them red against the current code. Then correct the docstring's second limit.
R2 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:728-775 (_case_callees, _case_label_nodes): The wrapper derivation mis-derives or misses common shapes. (1) A method wrapper, `def expect(self, name, ok): check(name, ...)` called as `s.expect('label', cond)`, is derived at position 1 because params include self. The CONDITION node gets marked as the label, and the real label literal is filed as 'other'. This is probe10 (e). (2) A label passed by keyword, check(label=...), or through a lambda or an imported helper, is never a label node. This is probe10 (f). With such an undetected wrapper, a generic label-argument template at HEAD ('%s is %s') refuses a genuinely new case: probe10 (g) gives exit 3 could-not-prove on HEAD but exit 0 proved on P82.2. That brings back round 1's R2 shape for these suites. (3) Callees are keyed by bare name and matched by attribute as well, so a derived wrapper named, say, `run` would mark `subprocess.run('...')` string arguments as labels. A read-only AST scan of this repo (plugins/audit/tests + tools, run once, not a gate) found no method wrappers and no keyword label calls. In this repo the exposure is therefore other projects' suites, which is where the label path matters anyway, since this repo's labels lead with ids. -> Offset the position by one when the def's first parameter is self or cls and the call is an attribute call. Also read a keyword whose name is the label parameter (`label=` for check, the derived param name for a wrapper). Only match an attribute callee by name when the name is not also a module attribute call, or restrict attribute matching to `_harness.*`. Add probe10 (e) and (f) as cases, and name lambda and imported-helper wrappers as a limit in _case_callees' docstring.
R3 (low) plugins/audit/tests/test_stamp_verification.py:1400-1405 (sr69), 1463-1467 (sr74); stamp-verification.py:421-435 (command_runner), 864 (held): Two mutations of the P82.3 code survive the full 90-case suite on a git-archive export of HEAD. Each mutated file was restored afterwards, and the unmutated suite printed ALL PASS: 90/90 cases passed. (1) `held = set(head['labels'])`: HEAD's other-role literals no longer count as held. This survives, but it turns probe10 (d0), an EXISTING table-fed case edited to go red, into exit 0 proved (checked on a scratch export). sr74 pins only the allow direction for table labels. (2) Dropping `-m pytest` from command_runner survives. In fact no case lets the command decide for pytest at all: sr69's pytest row expects None, because its echoed output carries no pytest summary. The CHANGELOG and the guide both name pytest as a runner the command decides. Mutations the orchestrator's table does cover (skip at 0 -> sr75 red; mixed picks the first tally -> sr55/sr69/sr70 red) reproduced here. -> Add a deny case: an existing table-fed case edited to fail, with no new literal, must stay could-not-prove. Add a command case: output with a pytest summary plus a house tally, under `pytest ...` and under `python -m pytest ...`, must read runner 'pytest', and the same output under a bare command must read mixed. Prove both red against the two mutations above.

tasks.title: red-first knows which cases HEAD already has by running HEAD's own suite, not by reading literals
tasks.description: Four review rounds each found a new corner in deciding "is this failing case the task's own" from the SOURCE of the test file (literal ranking, templates, roles, wrappers, bound names), and P82.4 still names limits that can produce a false proved. Replace the guess with a measurement. The throwaway tree at HEAD already exists; before copying the task's test files over it, run the SAME test command there on HEAD's own test files and record every case the runner names in that run, passing or failing (house PASS/FAIL labels, with a FAIL line's detail set aside as today; pytest node ids under -rA or -v; unittest test names). A failing case in the task's run is the task's own exactly when HEAD's own run did not name it. `--case` is checked against the same set. Fail closed: if HEAD's own run cannot be made or names no cases while its tally is non-empty, the verdict is could-not-prove with that reason. Remove the static literal-ranking machinery (_closest_literals, roles, _case_callees, templates, bound names) that this replaces - one mechanism, not two - and keep only what the measurement still needs. Keep every existing case that states a verdict (sr50-sr88 and the rest) passing or rewritten to the measured rule with a reason; the reviewer probes probe5-probe11 must all answer correctly. Record the cost of the extra run (timed twice with a gap). Update the guide, CHANGELOG, audit-executor.md and execute-task.md.

outcome.descriptive: Red-first proof now knows which tests already existed by running the previous version of the suite, so it cannot be fooled by how a test file is written.

tasks.title: red-first refuses the proof whenever HEAD's run and the task's run cannot be matched case for case
tasks.description: Round-4 review (review-P82d.json, probes probe12/probe13) found false proveds in the measured mechanism. The rule for all of them: a false proved must be impossible, so any case the two runs cannot be matched one to one is a refusal, never a credit. (F1) refuse when any case HEAD's run named is printed by the task's run in no label form (a label carrying a per-run value no longer lines up), and when a label is printed more often by the task's run than by HEAD's while one of those prints is a failure (F4: an edited case plus a new passing case of the same label). (F2) refuse when HEAD's run collected no case while a declared test file exists at HEAD, and when HEAD's run is red and may have stopped early (pytest 'stopping after' / 'Interrupted:', or a stop-first flag in the command: -x, --exitfirst, --maxfail, --sw, --stepwise, -f, --failfast). (F3) a declared test path that exists at HEAD but is absent from the working tree - a rename or a delete - makes the case set not comparable: refuse, and remove a deleted declared file from the throwaway so HEAD's put-back is exact. (F5) unittest names are qualified by class. (F6) HEAD's copies are restored byte for byte (git checkout HEAD -- <files>, or raw bytes). (F7) every git call of the put-back and the new-file check runs under the one deadline. (F8) _held_by_head's docstring and the guide name every limit that remains, all of them in the could-not-prove direction; the commit claim that said so falsely is corrected in this task's record. Each shape from probe12/probe13 as a red case, with the allow cases sr50, sr67, sr74, sr88, sr93, sr94 still proving.

tasks.title: red-first reads git paths exactly, re-checks reappearance after the fix run, knows every stop-first spelling, and bounds its pairing
tasks.description: Round-5 review (review-P82e.json; probes probe14-probe17). (1) every git path list is read NUL-separated (ls-tree -z, and any other name listing), so a quoted non-ASCII path is never taken as absent at HEAD; the put-back restores rather than deletes. (2) after the fix run settles an ambiguous line's label, reappearance of every HEAD case is checked again with the settled labels; a shorter reading no longer counts as reappearance when the settled label differs - a rename by appended ' (...)' is refused. (3) stop-first flags are recognised in every spelling a runner accepts: clustered short options (-vf, -fv, -v -cf), unambiguous long prefixes (--failf, --exitf, --maxf, --stepw), and pytest -x inside clusters; and when HEAD's run is red and the command is not a direct runner invocation whose every option the tool reads (sh -c, make, a wrapper script), the verdict is could-not-prove with that reason. (4) the pairing is an iterative Hopcroft-Karp (no recursion) under the one deadline; an overrun is could-not-prove, never exit 1; a size case over many identical and many distinct labels finishes inside the budget. (5) the docs claim only what holds: no false-proved limit is stated as could-not-prove, the 'has none of them' sentence goes, introduced() runs its git calls under the deadline, and the budget comment counts the runs truly made. (6) sr45's label states the measured rule and the case can go red on it. Each probe14-17 shape as a red case; the allow cases still prove.

tasks.title: red-first proves only against a green, isolated baseline, and every failure then is the task's own
tasks.description: Seven review rounds each found another way to credit a case past a RED baseline (probe20 (A), (C) this round). Every one of them depends on crediting while HEAD's own run is red, so the rule changes instead of growing another reader. New rule, one mechanism: (1) the task's tests run against HEAD's code and must be red with an assertion failure (as now). (2) HEAD's own test files run against HEAD's code in an ISOLATED checkout - a clean throwaway (checkout -f of HEAD plus clean -ffdx, so nothing the task's run wrote survives), PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, its own TMPDIR - and must be GREEN: a tally, no failure, no error. Anything else is could-not-prove with the reason "the command is already red (or unreadable) at HEAD - narrow it to the task's cases". (3) the task's tests run against the working tree's code (the fix run) and every case that failed in (1) must pass there; otherwise could-not-prove. (4) with (2) green, every failure in (1) comes from the task's change to the tests, so all of (1)'s failures are the task's own; --case must name one of them. Remove what this makes unnecessary - label matching and pairing (compare_runs, changed_reds, _uncovered, _hopcroft_karp and its SCC pass, the stop-first readers) - keeping one mechanism. Rewrite or remove the cases of removed functions with a reason each; every probe (probe5-probe21) must answer correctly, and a red baseline must now read could-not-prove with the narrowing reason. The docs, audit-executor.md and execute-task.md state the new rule and the narrowing instruction.

tasks.title: red-first always runs the baseline with the task's new test files as empty stubs, and credits only a failure located in a declared test file
tasks.description: Round-9 review (review-P82i.json; probe23, probe24). (1) baseline_skip read argv and was evaded by a second argument, a wrapper, a node id, a glob, a working-tree/HEAD mismatch. Remove the argv reader. HEAD's baseline is ALWAYS made, in its isolated throwaway, with every declared test file that is new at HEAD laid over as an EMPTY file and nothing else of the task's, so the same command reaches exactly what the task's run reaches minus the task's cases, however it is spelled. Green = exit 0 with no failure counted, or the runner's own no-tests-ran shape (unittest/pytest exit 5, nothing collected). Delete baseline_skip and the 'no HEAD run' basis. This also ends the over-refusal where a command naming a new file and an edited old one could never get a green baseline. (2) A new test file that imports or subclasses HEAD's cases carries them into its run. Credit only a failure the runner locates in a declared test file: pytest's node id path; unittest -v's module (3.11+ prints it); a house run whose command runs exactly one declared test file. A runner output that locates no failure is could-not-prove with that reason. (3) sr139 measures with tracemalloc, not the resource module (absent on Windows, which CI runs). (4) sr134 and sr135 pin E_NOT_RED and the note; sr140's replacement rows cover a dotted name, a node id into an old file and an sh -c script. (5) No further isolated run is made once less than a second of the deadline is left; the budget comment describes the code. Each probe23/probe24 shape (E1, E2, E2s, E3, E6, node id) a red case proved first; an allow case in sr138's shape (a command naming only a new test file) still proves, now with a stub baseline. The four documents state the rule the code enforces.
